desk_read: Yesterday's session was characterized by a clear split between energy complexes facing long liquidation and recovering equity and metals markets led by new longs and short covering. WTI Crude Oil saw prices fall -1.83 percent alongside a -1.2 percent drop in total open interest as volume ran at 1.0x its 20-day average under backwardation. Meanwhile, Natural Gas posted a price decline of -0.60 percent with total open interest contracting -1.4 percent in contango. In contrast, Copper attracted fresh participation with prices climbing +1.69 percent alongside a +0.7 percent rise in total open interest, signaling new longs. Similarly, the S&P 500 advanced +0.57 percent while total open interest crept up +0.1 percent, matching a contango structure.

Brent dropped -1.20% with total open interest down -2.4k contracts (-1.9%) and volume at 0.9x its 20-day average, also showing long liquidation within a backwardated curve where the BZZ26-BZK27 spread stood at +17.79 $/bbl.
